We are utilizing Skype for Business with Enterprise voice through a third party hosted provider. We use it for messaging, conferencing, video and voice calls. We can also communicate with external Lync/Skype for Business and Skype Consumer users.

We had an on-prem deployment prior and it was awful because we had no one qualified to maintain it properly.

I would recommend a hosted provider though it can be a little salty for a smaller business.

Do you have any advise for survival as someone whos completed the IB?

WOOOOOOOW you guys have a comp sci class? I would've killed to take HL computer science, or any computer science in high school. Basically my advice is take it a day at a time. Don't overthink or get anxious about the work ahead of you, but just focus on the work in front of you and you'll be fine. I was able to juggle my IB work with doing theatre outside of class, which is a huge time commitment, I just had to organize myself properly. Having been through that, I'm confident that anybody can take on the IB, so long as they tell themselves they can.

We are the first year that was able to take the course at our school after we spent two years basically asking for it and showing that there was a demand for it, I am really glad that we did too as its one of my biggest interests and something that I am looking to possibly study further in uni. Loving that, plus the exams were easy to any who was at all tech savvy so can't complain :)

I am working on most my IA's and Extended Essay at the moment and that is something that is a little worrying but I am taking it a little at a time and hoping that I am going to be fine. I got the bulk of my extended essay out the way but could do with some critic on it before I continue (also doing that on computer science). I can really sense though that time management is key with the way the workloads are!

If I may ask what did you did and subsequntly with the points you got did you find it easy to get into higher education (if you tried) using IB as its rather uncommon in most places.

Alright so unless I'm forgetting something, my full breakdown was:

HL English HL History of the Americas HL Theatre SL Biology SL Math Studies AB French

I ended up with 31 marks total. Not very close to 45, but it's well over what you need to pass. Fours, fives, and sixes in all of them (not that I remember the specifics) and I think I got 1 mark for my EE. I grew up in Florida and go to Florida State, and luckily most state colleges here recognize IB classes. I ended up going into college with 36 credits, and I need a total of 120 to graduate, so IB really helped me out because I knocked out over two semesters of work. My girlfriend wasn't so lucky though, because her college doesn't recognize IB credits, and so she didn't go in with anything extra even after all the work she put up with in high school.

So I guess you really just have to do your research when applying, especially in the US where IB credits are still just starting to become more commonplace. If you're applying to the right place, IB classes look great on an application and the credits will help you immensely. If you don't apply to a place like that...at least you have the memories.

I am looking to go to the UK so I am not sure if its similar or not however I will make sure I do my research. I think in the UK some places really value IB where as others don't recognise it much so looking for a uni that does seems important. Thanks for the lengthy reply!

No problem! Always glad to help. I can't really speak for universities over in the UK, but from what I've heard, IB credits are much more well-known and recognized across the pond.

One last random piece of advice I just thought of, in regards to your IAs and EE. Something I learned while looking through past exemplar papers is that the format is oftentimes more important than the content. Not saying to skimp on your research or writing, but it's extremely important you format it the way you're instructed to. A shitty paper with good formatting may score more marks than a phenomenal paper with awful formatting.

That is a point the has been put across though the year that I have done, especially with the TOK presentation that I am currently working on we have seen examples of incredible presentations that scored horrendously due to them not following the format which the examiner was looking for. Will be doing everything in my power not to make that mistake :)

I have just ordered the parts for my first 250 class quadcopter. Any tips for a noob?
Any tips for a quadcopter noob?
Start slow and when in doubt, but power :) Also, I heard good things about using tags they use for animals with gps. In case yoru quad decides to go sailing into the night.

A good tag I've heard is Tile you sync it with your phone's bluetooth and you can use your phone to search for it later (get within a 100' and it starts beeping loudly)

I'd say add a nano qx as a trainer - nearly indestructable and super fun to fly. has a safe mode with auto leveling to learn orientation on, and can also go into acro mode where you can learn acrobatics. I've literally flown mine straight into a brick wall to show people how durable it is. If your transmitter is spektrum or compatable you can get the copter itself for just $70 and bind to it.

250 class should be very durable - but i've heard props break all the time.. buy lots of spares and bring the tools to change them.

Same as MaryJanesBestBud said - start slow. get just high enough where you're not in ground effect anymore and slowly fly around.

also - flite test released a good video on getting oriented and started with multi-rotors - Here

Be careful and have fun.
